specimenDefinition.presentation: three-dimensional intact cell with an optional pedagogical cutaway
excludedStates: myelocyte or other immature granulocytic precursor

restingSuspensionDiameterMicrometres.basis: Primary optical-stretcher measurements reported 10.39 +/- 0.19 micrometres for 322 resting primary human neutrophils; the wider display range allows normal biological and preparation variation.

scaleAndShape.restingShape: approximately spherical in suspension, not a flattened blood-smear silhouette
scaleAndShape.mechanics: viscoelastic and strongly deformable; surface geometry may include restrained folds or microridges that provide membrane reserve
scaleAndShape.cutawayScalePolicy: Membrane thickness, chromatin bridges, granules, vesicles and glycogen cannot all be simultaneously rendered at literal scale. Any enlargement must preserve relative hierarchy and be described as pedagogical, not quantitative.

requiredAnatomy.label: Plasma membrane
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: One continuous, closed, deformable boundary enclosing the entire cell. It must not read as a rigid capsule or a second cell wall. Subtle folds or microridges are acceptable; large permanent spikes are not appropriate for the resting state.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: Thin translucent boundary with restrained surface relief. Any visible thickness is pedagogically enlarged.

requiredAnatomy.label: Cytoplasm
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: Continuous volume between the plasma membrane and nucleus, densely populated by granules but not fully occluded. It must remain visibly distinct from the nucleus.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: Pale, low-saturation, slightly translucent material. Granularity should come from discrete organelles and restrained microtexture, not from an opaque noisy shader.

requiredAnatomy.label: Segmented nucleus
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: A single nuclear system made from interconnected lobes. It is a logical parent for nuclear-lobes and chromatin-bridges and must never be represented as multiple independent nuclei.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: Condensed chromatin should read darker/denser than the cytoplasm, with modest internal heterogeneity rather than a uniform glossy solid.

requiredAnatomy.label: Nuclear lobes
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: Use three or four irregular, unequal lobes as the canonical individual specimen. Two to five lobes is normal mature variation. Lobes should form a compact, gently curved array within the cell and must not resemble a flower, chain of identical beads or separate nuclei.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: Dense, heterochromatin-rich lobes sharing the nucleus material family.

requiredAnatomy.label: Chromatin bridges between nuclear lobes
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: Every adjacent lobe must be joined by a continuous narrow DNA/chromatin-containing nuclear segment. Bridges may taper and curve but must not float, break, or look like cytoplasmic cords.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: Same chromatin/nuclear-envelope family as the lobes, with a minimum renderable diameter clearly labelled as enlarged for visibility.

requiredAnatomy.label: Primary (azurophilic) granules
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: Numerous membrane-bound submicrometre granules distributed through the cytoplasm without intersecting the nucleus or membrane. Use a heterogeneous size distribution; do not define identity solely by size because primary and secondary populations overlap.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: Visually distinguishable as a population from specific granules, preferably slightly denser/darker in cutaway view. The palette is a teaching code, not a claim that living granules are literally purple or black.

requiredAnatomy.label: Secondary (specific) granules
requiredAnatomy.geometryContract: Numerous membrane-bound submicrometre granules intermingled with the primary granules throughout the cytoplasm. Use heterogeneous size and distribution, with no artificial radial layers or perfect lattice.
requiredAnatomy.appearanceContract: A second restrained teaching-code material, typically lighter or less optically dense than the primary-granule material. Do not imply exact biochemical identity from color alone.

optionalOrSubvisualAnatomy.contract: Mature neutrophils contain gelatinase/tertiary granules, but their morphology overlaps the peroxidase-negative granule continuum. If included, render as a subtle minority population and do not claim reliable identification by shape or color alone.

Secretory vesicles are supported by subcellular fractionation and proteomics. If shown, use small sparse vesicles near and throughout the cytoplasm; they must not dominate the silhouette or be confused with granules.

Human neutrophil-rich leukocyte preparations contain approximately 20 nm glycogen particles. At whole-cell scale they should be omitted as discrete spheres or represented only by restrained cytoplasmic microtexture; conspicuous glycogen boulders are inaccurate.

optionalOrSubvisualAnatomy.decision: biologically present but not a prominent textbook decoration
optionalOrSubvisualAnatomy.contract: Primary human neutrophils possess a functional mitochondrial network, while neutrophil ATP production is strongly glycolytic and mitochondrial abundance/function differs from conventional textbook cells. Omit mitochondria from the core hotspot set. If included in a high-detail cutaway, keep them fine, low-salience and evidence-labelled rather than adding a few large bean-shaped organelles.

excludedOrDeemphasizedFeatures.reason: A mature neutrophil may retain a small Golgi region, but it is not an identity-defining whole-cell feature and should not be enlarged into a generic textbook stack.

excludedOrDeemphasizedFeatures.feature: large rough endoplasmic reticulum network or prominent nucleolus
excludedOrDeemphasizedFeatures.reason: These are characteristic teaching decorations of biosynthetically active generic cells or immature precursors, not the defining morphology of a mature segmented neutrophil.
Azurophilic, specific and nuclear colors depend on preparation, stain and imaging modality. Color may encode categories but must be documented as semantic coloring.
The resting cell is approximately spherical, but it is deformable and has membrane reserve; a polished rigid orb misrepresents its mechanics.
Granule populations are heterogeneous and dynamic. The model must not imply an exact count, exact diameter distribution or complete biochemical classification.

integrationRules.hotspotPolicy: Hotspots bind to the stable semantic IDs above. Individual lobe and bridge child names are allowed for selection/debugging but learner content should normally target the aggregate nuclear-lobes or chromatin-bridges IDs.
integrationRules.groupingPolicy: nucleus is the aggregate parent of nuclear-lobes and chromatin-bridges; azurophilic-granules and specific-granules are population groups, not individual hotspot-per-granule inventories.
integrationRules.materialPolicy: All educational colors require an in-scene legend or metadata note stating that they are semantic colors and not literal living-cell coloration.
integrationRules.statePolicy: Any animation that polarizes, migrates, phagocytoses, degranulates or forms a NET is a separate state/configuration and must not silently alter the resting reference geometry.

acceptanceChecks: The intact exterior is a continuous closed surface with real three-dimensional depth from every view.
The canonical nucleus has three or four visible lobes and every adjacent lobe is continuously connected by a chromatin bridge.
No lobe reads as a separate nucleus or floats in cytoplasm.
Both azurophilic-granules and specific-granules are present as intermingled heterogeneous populations.
Granule identity is not claimed from size or color alone.
No prominent generic Golgi, rough-ER or oversized bean-shaped mitochondrial decoration competes with the defining neutrophil anatomy.
Any cutaway exaggeration is disclosed and the uncut cell still passes the all-around geometry gate.
The semantic IDs exactly match semanticPartNamesExpectedByIntegration.

evidence.citation: Ekpenyong AE et al. Mechanical deformation induces depolarization of neutrophils. Science Advances. 2017;3:e1602536.
evidence.supports: Resting primary human neutrophils are approximately spherical in suspension; measured diameter 10.39 +/- 0.19 micrometres; whole-cell shape is mechanically deformable.

evidence.citation: Morikis VA et al. Atrial natriuretic peptide down-regulates neutrophil recruitment on inflamed endothelium by reducing cell deformability and resistance to detachment force. Biorheology. 2015;52:447-463.
evidence.supports: Primary human neutrophil viscoelastic deformation, cortical tension/viscosity and recovery toward spherical shape after micropipette aspiration.

evidence.citation: Rice WG, Kinkade JM Jr, Parmley RT. High resolution of heterogeneity among human neutrophil granules: physical, biochemical, and ultrastructural properties of isolated fractions. Blood. 1986;68:541-555.
evidence.supports: MPO-containing azurophil/primary and lactoferrin-associated specific/secondary granules, intact membrane-bound profiles, overlapping size/density and substantial heterogeneity.

evidence.citation: Rorvig S et al. Proteome profiling of human neutrophil granule subsets, secretory vesicles, and cell membrane: correlation with transcriptome profiling of neutrophil precursors. Journal of Leukocyte Biology. 2013;94:711-721.
evidence.supports: Fresh human neutrophil granule subsets, secretory vesicles and plasma-membrane fractions; validates multiple granule/vesicle compartments while cautioning against a simplistic two-shape inventory.

evidence.citation: Sanchez JA, Karni RJ, Wangh LJ. Fluorescent in situ hybridization analysis of the relationship between chromosome location and nuclear morphology in human neutrophils. Chromosoma. 1997;106:168-177.
evidence.supports: Typical mature human neutrophil nuclei comprise three or four heterochromatic lobes joined by thin DNA-containing filaments.

evidence.citation: Campbell MS, Lovell MA, Gorbsky GJ. Stability of nuclear segments in human neutrophils and evidence against a role for microfilaments or microtubules in their genesis during differentiation of HL60 myelocytes. Journal of Leukocyte Biology. 1995;58:659-666.
evidence.supports: Mature human neutrophils have three to five interconnected nuclear lobes; thin connectors elongate during migration but remain continuous.

evidence.citation: Shen C et al. Nuclear segmentation facilitates neutrophil migration. Journal of Cell Science. 2023;136:jcs260768.
evidence.supports: Direct imaging of primary human neutrophils links nuclear lobe number/segmentation to migration through narrow channels.

evidence.citation: Scott RB, Still WJS. Glycogen in human peripheral blood leukocytes. II. The macromolecular state of leukocyte glycogen. Journal of Clinical Investigation. 1968;47:353-359.
evidence.supports: Electron microscopy of human leukocyte preparations composed chiefly of neutrophils found approximately 20 nm glycogen particles; supports inclusion only below whole-cell visual scale.

evidence.citation: Fossati G et al. The mitochondrial network of human neutrophils: role in chemotaxis, phagocytosis, respiratory burst activation, and commitment to apoptosis. Journal of Immunology. 2003;170:1964-1972.
evidence.supports: Live human neutrophils possess a functional mitochondrial network; mitochondria should not be declared absent.

evidence.citation: Maianski NA et al. Functional characterization of mitochondria in neutrophils: a role restricted to apoptosis. Cell Death and Differentiation. 2004;11:143-153.
evidence.supports: Human blood neutrophil mitochondria are present but contribute little to ATP synthesis compared with conventional oxidative cells; supports low visual salience rather than generic textbook prominence.

evidence.citation: Al Jumaa MA, Dewitt S, Hallett MB. Topographical interrogation of the living cell surface reveals its role in rapid cell shape changes during phagocytosis and spreading. Scientific Reports. 2017;7:9790.
evidence.supports: Live-cell membrane diffusion measurements and correlated electron microscopy support a wrinkled/microridged surface and membrane reserve in round neutrophils.

limitations: This contract defines one representative mature resting human neutrophil, not the full biological range of neutrophil age, activation state, disease phenotype or tissue adaptation.
The canonical three- or four-lobed nucleus is representative; a normal individual neutrophil may have two to five lobes.
The two highlighted granule groups are a teaching simplification. Human neutrophil granules form heterogeneous subsets/continua that also include gelatinase granules and secretory vesicles.
Organelle colors, transparency and enlarged submicrometre structures are visualization conventions, not literal appearance or quantitative histology.
Glycogen evidence cited here used leukocyte suspensions composed chiefly, but not exclusively, of neutrophils and is therefore used only to justify a subvisual/optional treatment.
Mitochondrial organization in neutrophils is experimentally supported but remains context- and method-sensitive; it is intentionally not an identity-defining hotspot in this whole-cell asset.
